synopsis: OpenUSD and Omniverse offer domain-neutral scene, material and asset representation suitable for mines and construction sites, combining an open standard with NVIDIA components [f16001, f8610, f9167]. They can represent sites but are not themselves a validation method; sensor-material semantics and portability between simulators require governance [f9168, f8611]. Omniverse documentation includes an ultrasonic sensor extension, but the corpus did not find frame-rate figures for NVIDIA DRIVE Sim/Omniverse or several other simulators [f3942, f4957]. Licensing also needs review: some Isaac Sim assets, materials and Omniverse components have additional terms, despite the presence of an open-source core [f8486, f8908]. OpenUSD is listed as the interface and standard, while latest-release status is recorded only as “ongoing,” rather than a specific release [f9169, f9171].

relations.note: Both describe the combination of an open standard and vendor components.
Both describe domain-neutral scene representation; Chapter 11 adds materials, assets and site examples.
Both flag additional licensing terms for Isaac Sim assets and Omniverse components.
Identifies OpenUSD as the interface and standard underlying the combined tooling.
Limits scene-representation capability: it does not constitute a validation method.
Explains the representation capabilities of one listed environment-creation offering.
Using these scene representations requires governance of sensor semantics and simulator portability.
